approach: From the Bank day-use lot, walk into The Bank to the 2150 Wall trailhead and follow that trail until a branch peels off east at the Gem Wall sign. Continue east through The Bank, pass through The Vault, and cross the drainage to reach the base of Cactus Cliff, which sits to the northeast.

From the campground just before the entrance station, walk south through it to its far end and pick up the wilderness trail. Follow it up and down for roughly two hours to a signed turn for Lincoln Lake, then go right (west) about 1 mile to the lake's east shore. Circle the southwest shore to the west side, where the talus and boulder field rises to the west.

From the pullout at the top of the guard rail, take the trail down the ridge to a small saddle with an old campsite, continue straight and slightly right to regain the trail, and keep descending past rock outcrops on your left. Where the trail switchbacks down the west slope, drop into the third-class gully; the first wall you meet, the red north face on your left, is Neptune.

From where you leave the car, walk left of the wash along a bench on a good trail until you drop back into the wash. Where it forks, go left, then quickly cut steeply right to another bench and follow the well-worn trail to the base near Hand Solo.

Take the East Face Trail (blue blazes) up from Roy Gap Road, past the Southeast Corner, until you are above Gunsight Notch. A blue-blazed spur branches left; roughly 80 yards along it, climb a 10-foot step onto a ledge, traverse left on a dirty shelf and go up easy third-class steps to Upper Broadway Ledge, beneath Castor and Pollux.

A trail leaves the lot's north end, passes a notice board and switchbacks up through the forest. It bends back toward the cliff and tops out at the north end of Logger's Ledge, below the upper routes.

From Eldorado Springs, head south past old stone pillars and climb a trail to an aqueduct, then follow it south to a dirt road. Go up the road briefly, take a trail near its end through meadows and pines to a broad saddle, and continue west into a canyon. A faint trail climbs to the railroad tracks and Industrial Wall; keep going along the cliff to the wall. About 2 miles.

From the lot, walk east to the rim and go a short way upstream along it, passing the ranger house, until a steep scramble drops down. When the angle eases, continue upstream over boulder talus toward the first big buttress, Wildfire Wall.
From the large lot, follow the old mining road that starts just north of it and heads west, then continue up to the wall. Allow about 45 minutes.

From the Twin Owls lot, head west on the Black Canyon Trail. At about the one-mile mark, just short of the park boundary sign, an unsigned spur goes right; take it up through the trees to the signed junctions and follow the Bookmark Trail to the formation.

From the designated parking, walk straight back over the small creek and up the hill to the foot of the 5.10 Wall. For the other routes, follow the gravel road uphill until stairs appear on the right; they lead up to the foot of the 5.11 Wall.
From the Squire Pass trailhead, hike the trail up to the toe of the rock, then scramble steeply up to the Big Tree area. Higher, the trail carries on toward the North Buttress and Squire Creek Pass.
From the pullout, walk in to the clearing beneath the Shining Wall. Where the trail splits there, take the right-hand branch, which ends at the Hardscrabble Wall.
From the first pullout, follow the Grand Circle Trail west toward the second pullout, cross the wash, then cut back to the right over flat-topped sandstone ridges to reach the varnished wall.
Walk down to the bridge below the wall and take the staircase that rises directly above it up to the cliff base.

Cross the river on the bridge below the main parking area, turn right, and follow the bank around the river's northernmost bend. Hike up the gulch between Staender Ridge and the Student Wall to the irrigation canal, follow the Burma Road to its prominent switchback, then climb a rough trail uphill to Koala Rock.

Take the main trail for about 15 minutes to a Y and go right. Continue roughly a quarter mile beyond the cable warning signs to a second fork just past the Bonnie and Clyde sign, and go right again. About 5 minutes on, a large downed log lies across on the right; step over it at its midpoint and drop about 100 feet downhill to the Gun Show.

From the pulloff, walk back along the road about 150 feet to the signed trailhead and follow the trail uphill past boulders. At the obvious sharp right turn a faint trail leads left to the first few routes; for the main pinnacle stay on the trail to a fork, where either branch loops around the tower.

Start at the lot's west end, cross the road and take a short trail that winds up around the prow of a buttress. The first cliff you reach is El Diablo Wall; a contouring trail continues west over scree to Hell Wall and Hell Cave.

From the parking lot, hike the wide groomed main trail about 0.3 mile, passing the first posted climber's trail on the left. Continue another 0.2 mile to a marked climber's trail on the right, which leads to Cactus Flower East.

Take the well-worn trail that leaves the west side of the big lot and winds down toward the water. The dirt path ends at the Main Rock; side paths branching left and right drop you to the bolted lines at its foot.

From the ranger station at Chautauqua, walk up the old paved road on the south side, past the Bluebell Shelter, then follow the signs for the Second and Third Flatirons across a talus slope to a fork. Stay on the Third Flatiron Trail and you pass right by the BBC Boulder and the lower Satellite boulders.

Reach the Mesa Trail by either branch of the Shanahan trail. From the Mesa Trail, walk west up the wooded draw of Shanahan Canyon, following a faint path to the talus below the south face, between the Sphinx and South Shanahan Crag.
From the large parking area, take the short trail that starts just north of the lot. It leads to the Meat Wall, which sits east of the road.

From the end of the short side road, pick up the Lake Blanche Trail beside the outhouse, go to its first bridge, then branch right onto a path along the west side of the stream. Follow it uphill about a quarter mile to a talus slope under the Millstone and scramble up the stable talus to the base.
Where the spur road heading south dead-ends, hike a short way to the dome. The walk takes about ten minutes.

Starting at the roadside parking, go along the road until the second clear path on your left, flanked by a pair of boulders. Follow it through the woods, keeping the huge Cote Boulder on your left, to the blocks below the Mordor Wall.
From the main lot, take the nearest trail heading up and to the left toward Castle Rock. A short uphill walk of about 15 minutes brings you to the rock.

Starting at the trailhead lot south of the campground, follow the trail southward up into the saddle that separates Turkey Perch from Turkey Rock, then turn east to reach the base of the south face of Turkey Perch.
From the lot, follow the trail toward the lake. It runs northeast; stay on it until you can scramble down to the foot of the rocks.

Starting at the main roadside parking, go along the road until the second clear path on your left, which has a small sign on a tree. Take the path through the woods past the immense Cote Boulder to the blocks below the Mordor Wall, then bear left and scramble steeply uphill beside the cliff foot to reach the face.

Take the public access trail, head toward the rim and turn left onto the path nearest the edge. Follow it northeast along the rim about 150 yards to a small knoll, the top of the crag. Continue a short way north, drop down the gully on the north flank through the rock bands, then swing south to the base.

Walk up the residential street about half a mile to the signed trailhead on the right, then climb the wide trail past a bench until a narrow path splits off sharply to the left. Skip the left fork, stay on the main path to the next fork, and turn right onto the abandoned road grade heading east; Canopy Crag lies along it.
Follow the Pony Express Trail and, just past the large boulders, cut right onto a small path that leads to the foot of the wall.

From the road, at the spot opposite the large dome across it, hike about 30 minutes through dense forest. The dome stays hidden until nearly there; swing around to its southwest side, where most routes lie.

Pull into the large turnout on the west side of the road just after the creek crossing, cross the road and walk straight to the wall. The Wasteland is the cave on your left, while a short trail running south takes you to The Nappy Dugout.

Leave the car at the pullout 200 yards west of Vampire Rock, then retrace your steps along the creek and wade across beneath the buttress's west corner. A good path at the base of the wall carries you across to Black Widow Slab, whose clean north side is the one to aim for.

Look for a faint trail climbing the embankment into the woods just before the guard rail, up the road from the parking area. Pass through a fern garden to a large low boulder where the trail splits, and take the right branch straight back into the drainage. Cross two gullies (a fallen log helps at the second), then skirt uphill below a low cliff band. Allow 15-20 minutes.

Cross the trestle from Write-Off Rock, then scramble up the rocky slope on your right. A trail from there leads to the cliff base, and the wall rises above the railroad grade about 100 m east of the trestle.

From the climbers' lot, follow the Near Trail toward the base of Sunshine Wall, then keep going west past gully #2 beside the Tilted Pillars for roughly a quarter mile to the Far End cliffs. Tomato Wall is the red columns between gully #3 and the chockstone gully.
Leave the car below the crag and climb the talus slope up to the base of the rock.
Leave the car at the overlook, walk over the road, and pass under the old bridge. A trail there leads up onto the top of the wall.

Start at Chautauqua and climb the paved road beyond the ranger cottage to Bluebell Shelter. Go north on the Bluebell-Baird Trail until the Third Flatiron access trail, then follow that west; it winds toward the Third Flatiron's northeast flank, where boulders begin to appear. Keep heading north through them until the Second Flatiron's base is in front of you.

From Chautauqua, hike roughly three-quarters of a mile south along Kinnikinic Road to Bluebell Shelter. A short distance northwest on the Bluebell-Baird Trail brings you to the signed trail named for the First Flatiron. Take it west up a steepening ridge, then swing north on a rough path to the base of the east face.
From the Twin Owls lot, take the northern of the two trails heading west. After about 50 yards a right branch leads to Little Twin Owls.

From the Martin's Fork lot, cross over and head back along the road toward the tunnel until you see the signed trail for Military Wall and Left Flank. Pass over the wooden footbridge and continue straight, ignoring the Military Wall fork that splits right about 20 feet later. Cross a creek on stepping stones, then climb the trail for a few minutes to the base. A second bridge means you have gone too far.
Park where a cliff band crosses the wash, then head south up the large drainage. The boulders sit hidden from view, a walk of 25 to 30 minutes.

Follow the base of the cliff to the far south end of the lower Wonder Wall, passing a gully and a short band of rock. The path scrambles up through that band onto a terrace. Return right along the cliff base, then scramble up and right to a slab with a bolt.

Begin at the top of the West Trapps lot and take the path to Trapps Bridge. Climb the steps and turn north, staying on this side of the bridge. In a minute or two, just beyond the big Hurdy-Gurdy Block, a huge roof overhangs the carriage trail.

Follow the main trail about 15 minutes to a Y, then take the right fork. Continue up the trail roughly a quarter mile to another fork just past the Bonnie and Clyde sign and go right again. Pass the big downed log on the right after about 5 minutes, and keep going another 5 to 10 minutes out of the trees to a small clearing below Headlight Point.

Starting at the Honeymooners' Ladder, take the upstream trail as it veers away from the cliff and descends, passing between two large boulders. The next big wall you reach, steeply overhanging on its left, is Snake Buttress. Scramble between its white face and a huge block resting at the base.

Take the Mallory Cave Trail, heading southwest from the Mesa Trail where the trail from the research-center lot meets it at the south junction. You pass Square Rock, then go under the north face of Dinosaur Rock before reaching Der Zerkle. Der Freischutz and The Hand are just beyond.
From the pullout just across the creek, step over the road and walk straight to the wall. The cave on the left side is the Wasteland itself.

Leave the Fern Creek lot and hike a quarter hour to the clifftop at Fern Point. Veer left on the rim trail for another quarter hour to the Honeymooners' Ladder descent. At the bottom, turn downstream (left) for five to ten minutes to Diamond Point.

Cross the big concrete bridge over the Snoqualmie River; the trail starts right after its far end. Step over the guard rail and go about 100 feet to the signed old telephone-line trail that angles up the hillside. Follow the main trail about 0.75 mile to a Y and take the right fork. Pass a muddy patch after some 50 feet, and the Gritscone Boulder sits several hundred feet off the trail on your right.
Leave from the first pullout south of the Little Baldy parking area. The rock is a five-minute hike from there.
From the Sandstone Peak trailhead, hike the Backbone Trail for about an hour to the Tri-Peaks Trail. Then follow the climbers' trail to Boney Bluff.

From the parking area, take the road to the right near the entrance, then a short trail on the left to a second road. Follow it downhill to the valley floor by a stream. Skip the first left that doubles back across the stream, and carry on to a field on your left. Cut through the field to a ford, and after crossing, bear left on the first trail uphill. It passes some stairs and arrives at the rock between The Sanctuary and Indy Wall; turn right to reach The Sanctuary.

From the south end of the state park lot, follow the paved road downhill to the lower boat dock. A trail runs briefly beside the river there, then rises across talus to the cliff band you can't miss. Most people arrive beneath the first route, Piece of Cake.
From the parking pull-off, cross over and take a trail uphill for under 100 yards to a low, broken cliffband called Lovers' Wall. A trail along its foot leads on to the other outcrops.

Follow the main trail up the wash to the point where the Gardener's Wall path cuts off across the wash, then continue a few more minutes to a big pointy triangular boulder right of the trail. Turn right (west) on the spur just past it and scramble over boulders across the wash. Pick up the good trail on the far slope; it passes behind Gardener's Wall and runs along the open ridge to the Thumb.

Hike the Mallory Cave Trail, which heads southwest from the Mesa Trail at the south junction where the trail from the research-center lot joins it. It runs past the bottom of the Finger Flatiron's east face and ends below the formation. For the south and west faces, fork left onto the Hand Corridor trail, which ascends the wooded gully separating The Hand from Der Freischutz.

From the North Rim campground entrance, walk east to the first cattle guard and turn left on a trail heading west to the head of SOB Gully. Drop southwest down the gully, watching for loose talus and poison ivy. The routes are on the first and second buttresses to the left; about 20 minutes of walking gets you there.
Park in the small valley, then climb the draw to the crest of a low ridge, about ten minutes. Head west a short way until the base of the rock is visible, then angle north straight across to it.
Where the rough dirt road becomes undriveable, leave the car at the second Y and hike over the desert, then uphill, to the steep varnished cliffs. Allow about half an hour.
From the cul-de-sac parking, hike west along an old dirt track. After a few minutes it dips and turns into a foot trail; follow that toward Black Velvet Canyon. The boulder sits along this trail.

From the roadside pullout, follow the trail to the clearing below the Shining Wall. Here the trail splits, with the left branch going to the Madrone Wall proper and the right to the Hardscrabble Wall.

From the big lot, follow the old rocky Storm Mountain Trail south. It skirts beneath a large talus slope, then climbs steeply through trees past some big pipes. About a third of a mile up, a clearing opens a clear view west to the crag; take the climbers' path that leaves to the right, dropping into brush, crossing the creek and winding through evergreens to the base.
Hike the approach trail until you stand under Lower Sunset by Sunset Super Crack. A brief fourth-class scramble uphill from there brings you to the foot of Middle Sunset Wall.

From the parking area, take the obvious trail over the railroad tracks and through the woods for roughly 100 feet to a stone amphitheater at the foot of the slab. Some routes start on the ground; others begin on the first tier, reached by scrambling a short chimney on the right.

From the North Pullout, walk downhill on the East Access road, cross the seasonal creek, and continue south as the road opens into a field. At the fork, bear left and uphill, passing the Sloping Joe Boulder, to reach the clearing beneath the Goat Cave.

From the roadside turnout, take the climbers' trail that heads straight back into the woods and climbs the Spires Gully. It ends high up at a notch, with Higher Cathedral Rock on one side and a taller wall behind.

Take the Mallory Cave Trail, which climbs southwest away from the Mesa Trail. It passes Square Rock, runs under the north face of Dinosaur Rock, then goes by Der Zerkle before reaching Der Freischutz. The Hand Corridor branches left up the wooded gully between Der Freischutz and The Hand to reach the south and west faces.
Follow the Hidden Fawn Trail about 15 minutes to its junction with The Sisters Trail. Go 45 yards past the junction, then head up the hillside to the west for roughly 100 yards to reach Energy Crag.

Take the same walk as for the Goat Cave: from the North Pullout, down the East Access road, past the creek and field, and left uphill beyond the Sloping Joe Boulder to the clearing below the cave. From there a trail heads right and reaches the buttress in about five minutes.

Start on the Brookside/McCurdy Trail, number 607, from the Twin Eagles Trailhead. It winds through aspen groves and small valleys before a series of steep switchbacks gains nearly 2700 feet in about a mile; Crystal Tower sits about halfway up them. At the ridge above, the Lake Park Trail leaves to the right; stay on 607 through a marshy valley and over a small ridge, where it forks left and trail 628 goes north. The 400-foot tower faces west, just off the valley floor on your right.

From the lot, take the road on the right, then a short trail left onto another road that winds down to the stream. Turn left where the road doglegs over the stream, then continue past the Calvin Hollow sign and the Hideout turnoff to a second crossing. A few minutes on, a wooden sign on the right marks the trail, shortly before the road hairpins uphill. Follow it over a creek and through a marshy patch, then uphill to the wall's left side.

From the small dirt-road pullout, walk the dirt road about 60 yards, then at a cairn bear left onto the informal path up the wash. Short of some small, rugged limestone outcrops, the path veers left and scrambles up a steep scree hillside. Cairns mark the way over a small ridge and through a short third-class step to the Glass House.
From the Pizza Boulders area, hike southeast to the Checkerboard Wall.

Start at the trail across Fern Valley Road from the first big water tanks and head down the hillside, cross the creek, then climb to a paved road. Stay on that road until the pavement gives out. A climbers' trail then peels off northwest to the right and ends below the rock, close to the Buttress of Cracks.

From the Eagle Creek Canyon trailhead, take the trail toward Eagle Lake and hike all the way to the water. Beyond its west side, climb the obvious drainage to the ridge crest, then continue north to the base of the buttress.

From the Lake Study Area, turn right and follow the stream's left bank down-valley. The path switchbacks up and left to a big white boulder; pass it on the left and climb the eroded path straight uphill to the right end of the cliff, beneath Horner's Corner.
From the dirt pullout, head west along the dirt road for two miles. Where the road fades out, keep going up the increasingly rough canyon floor to the black wall.
From the Red Spring lot, pick up the trail that starts left of the boardwalk entrance, near the south restroom. Follow it to an old dirt track, then climb the hill on your right to the boulder.
Cross Tioga Road from the picnic area to the Murphy Creek trailhead and follow the trail up the drainage until an 80-foot cliff shows to the west. Leave the trail and walk across to its base.

Leave the parking area down the old road, then angle south onto the gravel saddle behind the dome. At the outcrop turn west and descend a short gully path to its west side; a spur branching left leads to the base.
Leave the lot on the obvious trail heading west, then turn north along it to reach the rocks.
Start up the trail that climbs from behind the muddy pulloff and bear left when it splits into two main branches. The left branch ends at the wall immediately to the right of the buttress.

Walk about 150 yards north from the lot, hugging the base of the west-facing cliff on your right and passing quarried blocks. After 50 more yards over slabs, turn east into the first corridor, go to its far end, and scramble about 100 yards up the drainage past a few pines.

From the small pullout marked by a cluster of towers beside the road, climb over the retaining wall between Andy's Hat and the others and pick your way down the steep slope; the first 50 feet are loose. Continue southwest down the gully, passing left of a large spire, until the taller faces of the towers appear on your left.

At the summit take the right-hand Down Road fork, where a boulder carries a painted sign. Slip past the pepper tree there and descend a steep scrambleway to the Triangles, then follow scrambleways north and slightly downhill to the right edge of the slab.
Start from the north side of the campground loop and walk northwest through the aspen forest, then grind up a steep talus slope to the base of the slab.

Take the approach to the West section, then keep climbing and curve rightward around the rock, passing the gully that leads to the top. The trail drops along the base, turns a corner and bends right into a grove of cedars near Mother Goose. Walk around the edges of the grove.

Follow the Blue Canyon Trail to the point where it begins to drop toward Blue Canyon (about 8600 ft); leaving it sooner means a slog through duff and brush. Head south-southeast to Point 8401 for views of the Middle Fork, then south and southwest over Point 7719 to the north base of the dome.
Park below the formation and work up the drainages a bit to the east of the rock, holding that side until the base is alongside you, then cut over. Allow 20 to 25 minutes.

From the AMC visitor center, hike the Tuckerman Ravine Trail for two miles, then bear right onto the Huntington Ravine fire road and follow it roughly another mile to the ravine. Continue up the Huntington Ravine Trail through the bowl to below the headwall. Pinnacle Gully and its waterfall are on the left, with Pinnacle Buttress forming the ridge beside it. Most parties need two to two and a half hours.
From the Angels Landing viewpoint parking area, ford the Virgin River, then scramble uphill to the foot of the cliff.
From the pullout by the southeast face of Peanut Gallery, climb the steep gully on the left side. At the top, pick up a faint trail that angles over to the right and ends below Space Wall.

From the Wild Basin trailhead, follow the trail past Copeland Falls, then leave it to the left (south), cross North Saint Vrain Creek and thread through the woods for about a tenth of a mile to the falls. They are easy to miss unless tracks show in the snow.

From the roadside, go through the gap in the fence and climb a gully roughly 300 yards. Watch for a tall ponderosa beside a huge boulder; an easy walk up the slope from there reaches the base of Window Rock.
From the Lumpy Ridge trailhead, take the Gem Lake Trail east and walk beneath the Twin Owls. Where the path swings around a tree-filled gully, veer left and follow the draw up to Gollum's Arch Rock.

From the Old Angler's Inn lot, walk upstream along the towpath about a quarter mile until a broken concrete culvert shows in the river. Take the path down to it, cross the river there, and follow the trails downstream along Sherwin Island. The crag sits back about 200 feet from the island's lower tip.
From the dirt pullout, cross the wash and climb the steep hillside to the broken brown cliffs, which face southeast. Allow about 20 minutes.
From the East Fork trailhead parking, follow the East Fork Trail northwest down into the canyon beside the river. Gateway Rock sits directly above the trail, about 100 yards from the lot.

From the Clear Creek parking area, follow the rim trail roughly 10 minutes toward the prominent canyon point and bear left just before it. After several hundred yards the trail splits; take the right branch and drop down a short step to the cliff base by Colorado Boy, then walk about 80 yards downstream to Image Wall.

Leave the main climbers' lot on the Near Trail and walk to the base of Sunshine Wall. Then follow the foot of the cliff west, passing the Near End and the King Pins, to reach the Tilted Pillars just beyond.
Hike up from the S-curves, skirting the toe of Lower Brother on its right-hand side. Third and fourth class ledges climb diagonally up and left to the base of the Absolutely Free routes.
From the roadside pullout, cross the road and take the established trail east through the trees to a long talus field. Climb the talus until you are level with Detox Wall; allow around 45 minutes.
Find the Brick Wall beside the road, then continue west on the same side and climb the southwest-facing hillside to the block. Count on about fifteen minutes.
From the lot, take the first path on your left, which heads toward the quarry. It meets the cliff right at the foot of Quarry Corner Buttress.

From the Sandstone Quarry lot follow the Calico Tank trail up the main drainage past Mass Production Wall, angling slightly right onto a path that contours the hillside. Where the red rock ends the path drops into a drainage; walk up it another 200 yards or so and the wall sits on your left, to the northeast.

Take the trail from the Sandstone Quarry lot about 200 yards to a huge white boulder. Pass it, go to the end of the small white cliff, and take the short steep path up to the ridge top on your left. Follow the ridge northwest for about 1000 feet, staying right of the canyon ahead; Sonic Youth Wall faces north on your left.

Follow the trail from the Sandstone Quarry lot about 200 yards to a big white boulder, pass the end of the small white cliff beyond, and climb the short steep path to the ridge top on your left. Walk northwest along it for about 1000 feet, keeping to the right of the canyon; the tall wall rises straight ahead on your right.

From the Round Pond parking area, walk past the Hill Boulders to the Lower Slabs, a couple of minutes away. The Cliff Boulders are right there, and the Font Boulder sits beside the trail that climbs onward to the Upper Cliff.

Head up the dirt road beside the power poles as it climbs the hill, and stay on it until a trail joins from the north. It leads to some square boulders. About 200 feet east of them, a trail drops down a steep, brushy slope to the base. Iron Curtain Wall is to the west, Riptide Wall to the east.
Take the Sam Hill trail but bear left early, then scramble up slabs and talus to the foot of the wall. Spot the white-streaked dome from the road first to line up your route.

Look uphill from the parking area, and enter the old forest just left of the swath of slide alder and vine maple. Follow a path up and left to the narrow boulder wash, which leads straight uphill to the crags, gaining about 1000 feet.
From the parking lot, hike the busy groomed trail about 0.3 mile to a posted climber's trail on the left. It leads to the AMC Boulder, passing Loafer's Choice on the way.

Follow the old dirt road trail past the pile of rocks holding Breaking Away and on through the open valley beyond. About 0.8 mile farther, a formation high on the hillside with parallel cracks facing the road is Hidden Dome. Scramble up for about ten minutes to its base.

Hike the West Ridge Trail past the Ranger Trail junction to the first sharp switchback, then follow a faint path south to a broad sandy saddle. Continue about 100 yards until the path leaves the ridge crest, then contour along the foot of the west-facing cliffs. Pebble Beach is the first big buttress.

From the big picnic area north of the visitor center, take the Inner Canyon Trail north and follow it down the canyon to the power lines crossing the gorge. Look for the Juggernaut Area on the canyon's north side, directly beneath the lines.
A brief trail from the parking area gets you onto the summit of the rock. To get down to the south face base, scramble around the rock on whichever flank suits you.
From the parking spot on the ridge top, hike east downhill to the river and wade across, then walk north along the far side to the rock. Allow about an hour.

From the Lily Lake visitor center, take the dirt road running south behind the building. Shortly before the barrier across it, turn east and climb through lodgepole pine, then keep east, bearing slightly north, through thick forest, deadfall and brush until you meet a long talus field, and follow it up toward the crag. It is barely a mile but about 45 minutes before you clear the trees.

Take the second approach trail, which starts at the far side of the main lot beside the kiosk, behind the garage. Drop down onto the valley bottom, ford the creek, then take the first left-hand path. Walk north a few minutes to the Washboard Wall sign on your left; the main wall is a couple more minutes along that spur.
Pick up the obvious trail climbing from the back of the large muddy pulloff. At the big fork keep right. That branch arrives at the cliff on the left side of the Undertow Wall, close to Madness Cave.

From the Pine Creek lot, follow the signed trail downhill and turn left (south) onto the Fire Ecology Trail until it nears the drainage. Cross the drainage, climb the far hill, and angle south over open desert on a faint trail into Juniper Canyon. Walk up the drainage until a large pale mound with a pine growing at its left splits it; the Rainbow Wall is on the left above.

From the Black Velvet parking area, head west along an old dirt track. After a few minutes it dips and narrows into a foot trail. Stay on that well-worn path toward Black Velvet Canyon; the Twin Towers boulders sit beside it on the way in.

From the Boulder Natural field, pick up the white-blazed trail behind Ride The Lightning and follow it toward the North Mountain summit. If starting at the parking area, swing sharply left after passing that boulder. After about five minutes The Premier appears on the left; the Walrus Boulder is the first big boulder above it, on a mound left of the trail across a wash.

Park at the end of Wasatch Blvd and walk up the dirt road beside the power poles until a trail joins from the north. It leads to some square boulders. About 200 feet east of them, a trail drops down a steep brushy slope to the foot of the routes. Riptide Wall is the eastern of the two walls.

Park at the turnout on the Road 2065 spur and hike the overgrown spur road about 10 minutes, then keep straight to the stream. Go upstream beside the creek, bearing right at every fork, then scramble to the foot of the wall. There is no real trail, so expect an hour or more.
Leave the car at the dam or the tiny turnout right below the cliff, cross the road with care, and hike up the stream gully. The cliff is about 100 yards above the road.

From the first parking area, the Kaymoor Miner's Trail drops steeply to a set of steps between The Hole and First Buttress, in under ten minutes. At the bottom of the steps turn left along the Miner's Trail for roughly 50 yards, where a faint path branches off to the base of First Buttress.

From the Lily Lake visitor center, take the dirt road running south behind the building. Shortly before the barrier across it, turn east and climb through lodgepole pine, then keep east, bearing slightly north, through thick forest, deadfall and brush until you meet a long talus field, and follow it up toward the crag. It is barely a mile but about 45 minutes before you clear the trees.

From the south side of the small reservoir at road end, hike southwest about a quarter mile to the park boundary, then pick up a trail heading south to the crag. You can also start from the westernmost campsite and head southwest through open forest. The crag is hidden until you arrive.

Starting at the Bob Boulder among the Terrain Boulders, follow old trail beds straight south for about ten minutes, keeping to the base of the steep hillside on your west, to reach Mamoonious. On the way out, retrace this route rather than cutting east to the Mesa Trail.
From the Buchanan Pass trailhead at the end of the pavement, pick up the Buchanan Pass Trail by its signs. The Warm-up Area is one of the trail boulder groups along it.

From the parking loop at road end, take the trail on the right side of the loop and follow it about half a mile, over a small arch, to a buttress at the ridge end. You can rappel from a tree to the base, or avoid that by dropping left down a steep hill on a faint path from the small arch, then turning right under some small walls.
Take the obvious trail that climbs from the back of the large muddy pulloff. At the big fork bear left; this path reaches the cliff just to the right of Buckeye Buttress, near the GMC Wall.

Walk the main trail down from the lot and take the first path left, about 120 yards along. Follow it roughly 400 yards over a red outcrop, then down to a wash with a pine. The best staging spot is under an overhang at the right (east) end of the crag; expect some scrambling.

Go down the trail from the second pullout; the second left fork is yours, since the first heads to The Gallery. Cross a red sandy flat, bear right into a drainage, scramble about 100 yards to an open area, then continue west past the Sweet Pain gully to a bushy east-west gully. Follow that 50 yards, turn up the narrow gully on the right for 100 yards, and the wall is on your left.

At the fork, go left and continue uphill on the old logging road, ignoring side roads, to a cairned right turn before a small pond and swamp. Keep the swamp on your left and follow the flat trail to a 90 degree left bend; a cairn on the right marks the path into the woods toward Happy Valley. After about 200 feet turn right at a cairn, follow the cairns to a grove of evergreens, and drop down the corridor between two boulders. Sleeping Giant is around the corner to the left.
Scramble up the gully left of the wall until you can cut right across an easy face to the foot of the routes.

Park at the pullout by the stone bridge beneath the tunnel switchbacks, then follow the trail east up Pine Creek. Leave it to climb the talus slopes below The Fang to the routes, about 45 minutes in total.

Several ways in. Easiest: where the Moses Spring Trail meets the Monolith's north face, cut right on the path running between the cliff and the Monolith. Alternately, skirt the Monolith's east face past Subterranean Tango to the shady pit below Bridwell Bolts, then scramble boulders left of The Black Dagger.
Where the Mesa Trail meets the trail from the atmospheric research center at its southern junction, take the Mallory Cave Trail southwest. It climbs straight past Square Rock.

From Chautauqua Park take the Enchanted Mesa Trail, an old dirt road behind the auditorium, to the Mesa Trail, where the Woods Quarry Trail begins. Alternatively use the Tomato Rock Trail, which joins the quarry trail just north of the quarry.

From the North Rim Campground walk east along the road past the cattle guard, then turn south on a small trail into the woods and down Cruise Gully. Pass two sets of rappel anchors (two 120 ft rappels, or downclimb at 5.5), then scramble east up a short gully from the last rappel to the wall's base.

From the Twin Owls lot follow the Gem Lake Trail past its pronounced left bend. About 200 yards further, leave the trail where the crag's north face comes into view. The crag lies just north of Fin City.
From the Pine River Campground trailhead, hike some 13 miles to the Flint Creek drainage where it meets the Los Pinos River. Then follow the river 2 miles upstream to the foot of the 1,200 ft wall.

From the parking area take the road that starts to the right near the entrance, then a short trail left onto a second road that winds down to a stream in the valley. Turn left where it doglegs and fords the stream. A few minutes on, a signed trail for Calvin Hollow, Boneyard and MN Surf climbs left to the cliff; go left to a small slabby wall of bolted lines.

Leaving the lot, pick the first left-hand path toward the quarry and meet the cliff at Quarry Corner Buttress. Follow the cliff line up and to the left roughly 20 meters, then swing right through the gap between two boulders. The tower stands just beyond, with the cliff band behind it.

Leaving the lot, pick the first left-hand path toward the quarry and meet the cliff at Quarry Corner Buttress. Follow the cliff line up and to the left roughly 20 meters, then swing right through the gap between two boulders. Pass through the corridor between the cliff and Sun Drop II Tower, then step down through small boulders to Red Rock Buttress.

Head up the main drainage past Mass Production Wall, angling right to a trail that contours the hillside. Once past the red rock's end by roughly 200 yards, it descends into a drainage; carry on another 200 yards to Holiday Wall. From its right edge go 150 yards diagonally up and right, about 200 yards above the wash, to the corridor with the brown streak. Plan on about 25 minutes total.

From the parking, stroll west on an old dirt track, which sags and turns into the Black Velvet foot trail. As the path descends toward the wash and cuts through a red sandstone layer, you can see the boulder just across to the north.

Beyond the cul-de-sac an unofficial path runs north, crosses a deep wash and angles through a vacant lot where a house once stood. From there the Kraft Boulders come into view, and Heart and Sole lies a short walk on, 5 to 10 minutes in all.
From the roadside pullout, a trail heads south and climbs a hill to the Roadkill boulders.
From the Grotto picnic area, head southeast to a faint path that climbs brushy slopes to the foot of the buttress left of the giant arch.

Cross the road from the lot, step over the guardrail and follow the stream bank, then the woods, up to the railroad trestle. The trail passes under the trestle by the lower rock, loops back beneath it and climbs to the railroad grade and the upper rock.

Follow the cairned path up the gully below Warpath Dome, then keep following cairns southeast past the top of that gully. The path drops into the head of the next gully and runs straight at the wall, a low-angle face split by clean cracks on the far side.

From the Cathedral Lakes parking area, take the Cathedral Lakes trail for about half a mile, then fork left onto the rough Budd Creek path to Budd Lake, which sits below the Cockscomb and its neighbouring summits.
From the Whitney Portal trailhead, follow the Whitney trail to the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek path and climb alongside the creek up its narrow, brushy canyon toward the east faces.
Start up the Spires Gully climbers' trail into the woods. Where it swings into a clear diagonal up and right, leave it for a faint trail that heads straight uphill to the spire.

Take the climbers' trail up Spires Gully, which heads straight back into the woods and climbs steeply. It tops out in a gap separating Higher Cathedral Rock from the cliff above and behind it, where the spire's routes start.
From the road pullout, take the wooden stairs straight down to Butt Rock.
From the Echo Lakes lodge area, cross the lake outlet and walk west on the Pacific Crest Trail along the north shore. The first obvious cliff you meet is Echo Edge.
Start at the East Inlet trailhead outside Grand Lake and hike the East Inlet trail to Lake Verna. From the lake's east end, scramble up through the trees to the valley below the base of the Aiguille.

From the Twin Owls lot, follow the Gem Lake Trail around a pronounced left turn and on to the next turn, to the right. Leave the trail there and push fifty yards through brush to open slabs, and work up the small drain that separates Out West Crag from Crescent Wall. The fins perch at the top of that drain.
Park in the pullout and head up the valley on the trail. The first rock you see on your right is Redemption Rock; Java Dome and Bali Dome sit together where the valley ends.
From the roadside pullout, the dome is visible in the valley to the south. Pick the easiest way down to the valley floor and walk across to the foot of the rock.
From the Mesa Trail, walk about 60 feet north, then cut into the gully that angles northwest and uphill. Zoofarsus sits about seven minutes up the gully.

From the Pine Creek trail, leave the path near the old homestead and swing around the east end of the low red cliff band on your right. Continue up to the big cleft of the gully. Heading straight up through the middle of the band means dicey unroped scrambling, so go around. About 20 minutes.

From the Boulder Loop trailhead, follow the loop to a fork, then go straight rather than climbing to the top of the ledges. The Main Cliff appears on your left above a talus slope. Keep hiking about ten minutes beyond it and the right-hand end of the Far Cliff comes into view on the left.

From the last pullout at the far west end, walk south with the boundary fence on your right and keep it in view. Cross open rolling hills and small creeks, and ignore the fence where it bends west; keep heading south. From the last hill you spot the cliff ahead, facing west and coated in yellow lichen. Expect some bushwhacking along buffalo trails; about an hour.

From the Obsidian Trailhead follow the Obsidian Trail about 3.5 miles to a junction, then take the left fork roughly a mile to the PCT at Sunshine. From there, follow climbers' trails about 1.5 miles cross-country east, toward the Collier Glacier col, the northwest ridge or the Renfrew Glacier.

Take the Lake Blanche trail from the S-curve in Big Cottonwood Canyon, about three miles to the lake. From there, a scramble of roughly half an hour leads to the base of Sundial, the prominent peak just south of the lake.

Take the Mount Washington Trail up to where it switchbacks right, at the spot with alder logs laid across. Go left, straight ahead, on a fainter path and pass under a wall of shattered rock. About 50 meters beyond, a faint side trail climbs up and right to Chainsaw Wall. Allow about an hour from the railroad grade.

From Humber Park, take the Ernie Maxwell Trail across Strawberry Creek and around a bend, about 200 yards further. Turn onto a crude, steep path straight up the hillside on your left, keeping right of a talus field. It leads about 0.4 mile to Lunch Rock at the foot of the face.

Starting at Tioga Lake's western parking area, take the unmaintained trail into Glacier Canyon, then climb the dry drainage east onto the Dana Plateau. Cross to its northeast edge, where the pillar's top sits. Scramble down the steep ridge just north of it (class 3-4), then step over the snow-filled gully and work across to the topmost ledge, which holds the start.

Leaving the main parking area, walk the Saratoga Gap Trail westward over the creek. Where the trail splits just beyond, fork up and right onto the Ridge Trail. In about 10 minutes Billy Goat Rock is on your right, marked by a wooden fence running from a tree in front of the routes along the trail.

From the McCullough Gulch trailhead, follow the old road west and cross to the north side of Quandary Creek on the vehicle bridge. Stay on the road west until it switchbacks east, then leave it for a rough, rocky trail west. This climbs past a cascade to the eastern tip of a skinny lake sitting at 11,900 feet, 1.3 miles from the start.
No real trail exists. Walk to the Pear, then bushwhack uphill among the trees, staying west of Sunshine Buttress, to the dome perched high on the slope above.
From the Buchanan Pass trailhead at the end of the pavement, walk west up the very rough road. The roadside boulders, Bolt Boulder among them, sit along it.
Go up the Martinez Creek canyon as far as the concrete water control, then ford the stream to the west. Angle uphill and west toward the wall on the west side of the canyon, about a 15-minute walk.

From the lot, the first left-hand trail heads toward the quarry and meets rock at Quarry Corner Buttress. Follow the base of the cliffs up and to the left for about 20 meters, then cut right through a gap between two boulders. Squeeze through the corridor beside Sun Drop II Tower, and Wasp Haven Buttress is on the right.

From the dirt pullout 0.2 mile into the Willow Spring turnoff, follow the obvious trail about 300 yards, passing a spring, to the mouth of the canyon. Routes lie left (southeast) in the shade and right of the dry waterfall.

From the lot, head roughly 200 yards northwest, passing a pale boulder sitting in the big wash, to an old roadway that you follow a little over 300 yards until it ends. Leave the trail to the left and go about 500 yards up the wash, parallel to the Marshmallow, to the Twinkie. The Bull Market is the brown bulging formation up and right (northeast) behind the Twinkie.
From the small roadside turnout below the Pillar, cross the valley bottom and follow the trail that leads to the northeast face.

Cross the road from the turnout and take the sandy, eroded trail that climbs steeply to the base of Rattlesnake Rock, near the Viper Crack. Piton Tower, a free-standing pillar, stands farther left along the base.

Follow the trail toward Gardener's Wall, but instead of crossing the gully, keep going up it past Glass Dome to the saddle above. From the saddle, contour up and left across the barren slope to Goat Hill, on the south side of the ridge where Hog Heaven is.
The pinnacle is the tower directly uphill from the main Windy Point lot. Walk east about a minute to its base.

From the Cathedral Lakes parking area, hike about half a mile, then a sizeable unmaintained trail splits off left and tracks Budd Creek up toward Budd Lake. Head up the wide scree gully lying between Echo Peaks 7 and 8, then cross slabs to the foot of the crest.

Start up the Old Big Oak Flat Road from the wood yard service road west of El Cap Meadow: go straight up the hill to the main roadbed, which angles gently west. About 45 minutes of hiking brings you to a railing overlooking Last Resort Cliff.
Hike up from Happy Isles on the way to Little Yosemite Valley; Mount Broderick is the large rock directly west of Liberty Cap.

From the Split Rocks lot, head downhill to the northwest behind Split Rock, then bear right onto a well-worn path across the desert. Before long a tower split by a chimney comes into view: that is Frigid Tower.
From the Hidden Valley trailhead, walk into Real Hidden Valley. The rock pile is on your right as you go in.

From the Echo Lakes lodge and marina, cross the lake outlet and follow the Pacific Crest Trail west along the north shore. Echo Edge is the first cliff you meet; Flagpole Peak is the big face on the northern skyline, with the other formations spread in front of it and to either side.
From the Rockhouse Basin trailhead, hike across the South Fork of the Kern River to reach White Dome. Plan on about an hour and a half.

Starting at the South Crestone trailhead, head 100 yards east, then swing south over South Crestone Creek. The Willow Creek Trail leads you over a ridge and down into the Willow Creek drainage, then continue east up the valley, crossing the creek twice, to Willow Lake at 11,564 feet.

Start at Hoosier Pass and follow the rough jeep track west to the Magnolia Mine, around 12,250 feet. A foot trail then follows the long gentle ridge to the east end of the summit ridge; the true summit lies 1.3 miles of easy scrambling farther west.

Hike the Royal Arch Trail to where it starts climbing south out of Bluebell Canyon. At the first left switchback, a big boulder carries a painted Royal Arch sign with an arrow. Break right here onto a lesser trail and follow it until it dies out beneath the West Ironing Board; this way also serves the Ironing Boards.

From Chautauqua Park, cross the car-free Kinnikinic Road and take the Chautauqua Trail southwest over the open meadow. In the trees, turn left (southeast) briefly at the Bluebell-Baird Trail, then right onto the First and Second Flatiron Trail, which leads to the foot of the east face. The Spy Express trail forks north from there and runs beneath the First Flatironette.
From the Buchanan Pass trailhead at the end of the pavement, walk west up the rough four-wheel-drive road. The roadside boulders, Fingerbanger Boulder among them, are found along it.

From the dead-end parking at Chair Rocks, walk west down the old abandoned road about ten minutes to Spoof Rock. Continue roughly 100 feet further along it, then follow a game trail north, staying below the ridgetop rock, for about thirty minutes to reach Upper Gemstone.

Descend the trail from the lot into the wash, bear northwest (left), and work up the drainage for roughly 200 feet to where it steepens. A ship-prow rock splits the drainage; keep right at the fork and scramble roughly 300 feet uphill. The cliff is on your right.
From the pullout, walk into the Red Rock Wash, which runs off to the south of the dirt road, and follow it to the boulder. Expect about 15 minutes.

Take the main trail past the turnoff to the Y-12 area, cross a creek, and in about 15 minutes meet the old logging road again. Turn right along it to an obvious clearing, where a wide gully descends to the cliff base.

Start on the Bench Lake Trail, which loops through meadows past Bench Lake and drops into the Snow Lake basin. Hike to the lake's south end along its west shore, where the path ends, then work up moderately steep slopes out of the cirque onto a steep bench. Snow, or talus and heather late in the season, climbs to a low notch in the ridge near 6,500 feet.

From road's end, head up the canyon on an old alder-choked road. After about 10 minutes the path dips through hemlocks and crosses a stream on a small footlog; roughly 10 more minutes of forest lead over a rocky streambed to Copper Creek. Ford it, climb the talus beyond to a slabby waterfall, then follow the right bank into a narrow gully through slide maple to the base.

Hike the Mount Washington Trail from the railroad grade, about 10 minutes, to the first crag you meet, just short of the culvert crossing. About 100 meters above the first switchback, spot a log leaning on the hillside (two of them, the larger one hidden). Go 15 feet further, then push into the brush onto a steep muddy path that runs under the logs to the base.

Start at Calle Concordia's end and hike the Pusch Peak Trail, or walk east out of the El Conquistador resort, toward the northwest-facing buttress below the summit; the walk takes about an hour. The wall is marked by a huge red-brown roof on its right side. For the Crescent, follow the trail 2 miles to a waterfall and walk the cliff base left of it for 85 yards.

Leave the lot heading south on the Bell Rock trail for a few hundred yards, then scramble onto the slickrock and up the west-facing amphitheater between the two arms. Near the top take the right fork of the gully to a platform (exposed third class). Go left behind a small tower to a pass, then left along a ledge under the summit towers' northeast face to a notch.

Queen Victoria is the small spire across the wash, right of Pointed Dome. Drop into the wash, turn right and follow the broad trail on its far side about 300 yards to a small gully on the left. Climb it onto a bench below Moose's Butte, contour the right flank of the valley to the saddle gully, and follow it up to the saddle beside the spire.

Hike the Mount Whitney Trail about 8 miles from the portal to Trail Camp, a big bivouac area with campsites and a toilet. Muir is the obvious high point directly west, just north of Whitney Pass on the Sierra Crest. From camp, a talus hike leads to the base of its eastern escarpment.

From Atwell Mill Campground on Mineral King Road, follow the trail toward Paradise Peak until it fades out. After that comes a long bushwhack to a gully; it rises to the saddle separating the Spire from the Fin, so climb it to that notch.

From the Piney Lake parking area, follow the trail northeast. At 2.9 miles a cairn marks a faint climbers trail heading north on the west side of the stream; it is hard to follow in places. It climbs into the bowl between Mount Powell and Peak C at about 11,200 feet, then aim for the east couloir on the southwest ridge.

Starting at Needleton, get over to the Animas River's east bank and walk north to Watertank Hill, where cliffs push you upward. Over that rise, an easy stretch of about a mile brings you to Noname Creek. A good trail then leads four miles east to the basin, with camping near the creek fork at 10,800 feet.

Take the Red Rocks Trail north up its switchbacks to the first intersection, then turn left (west) onto the Morrison Slide Trail. Follow it to the top and across the plateau toward the north; the boulder sits at the north end of the plateau, just before the ground drops away.
Cross the stream and hike straight up the open forest to the foot of the north face. Alternatively, start beside Cob Rock's western flank and angle uphill and to the right.
Start from the roadside pullout directly beneath the rocks, across from a drainage. Follow the drainage steeply up toward the rocks, passing Poop Slab first and then reaching Poop Point.
Take the north trail around the back of The Slabbo to the saddle. That route brings you to the opening cluster of Boulder Pile formations, and it is the preferred way to get to Physical Face.
Pick up the Rock One Trail beside the water fountain at the Twin Owls lot's north edge. The path heads up the gully that separates Rock One from Rock Two, with cairns and red tape showing the way.
Follow the Cow Creek Trail from the trailhead for about 1.5 miles to the backcountry campsite on the south side of the creek. The rock stands just above the camp.

Walk north from the lot for about 150 yards, hugging the foot of the big west-facing cliff on your right and passing quarried blocks. Cross slabs a further 50 yards, then swing east into the Sandy Corridor, the first one. Go to its back end and scramble up the drainage for roughly 100 yards. Shortly before the red rock gives out on the canyon's north side, climb a ramp leftward to a pair of enormous freestanding blocks; the wall is the southwest face of the right one.

Leaving the pullout, go east along the divide, climbing shale ridges until the lower cliff band opens in a gap. Scramble up some ledges, then bear left across loose talus and boulder debris until you reach the cliff foot.
From the small parking area at the end of the upper road, follow the dirt-road trail up the valley. The boulder is about 200 yards along, on the east (left) side of the little creek.

From the lower Fish Creek Falls lot, follow the paved sidewalk beside the road toward the second lot. Turn left onto the rocky path heading north and stay on the main trail for a few minutes until it runs into the crag and the small blocks around it.

From the Gill Boulder, walk the upper road west about 100 yards to the Eldorado Canyon Trail. Climb two switchbacks, then stay on the main trail through nine more (the Rincon Wall cut-off is at the fifth). A couple of minutes past the last one, cross the grassy ridge above the Musical Boulders, turn east and climb 50 yards up a faint ridge to the block.

From the Falls trailhead, hike east down the trail, then turn south on the creekside path just past the wooden fence. Cross above the top of the waterfall, descend a brief slope, then climb a gully until you meet a faint trail running north to south. Head directly uphill from there to reach the Big Blocks Area, where the two Sentry blocks sit side by side.

From the Auxier Ridge lot, go back along the road for around 100 feet and then follow the old gravel road roughly half a mile to the third road on the left, just beyond the one to Star Gap Arch. Follow that trail half a mile past a pair of old campsites, then bear right along the ridge another half mile over some rocky stretches. When the orange buttress shows ahead on the right, go five more minutes and take a faint trail down to the wall.

From the Trail Canyon Trailhead, hike the Trail Canyon Trail for roughly a third of a mile (0.35) until a climber's path breaks left and climbs a steep hill to The Hood. Corrosion Cave is the first wall you reach. Expect 20 to 30 minutes from the parking.

From the Smith Rock footbridge, follow the river trail to the right for about a mile around the northern bend. Past Juniper Spire the path turns uphill in switchbacks to the first of the pinnacles; Staender Summit sits at the top of the ridge. Expect 30 to 45 minutes depending on how high you go.
Cross the footbridge and walk right along the river for about half a mile to a very large pine. Scramble a short scree slope uphill to the base of the pale-colored cliff. Allow about 20 minutes.

Park at the northern end of Park Avenue by The Organ and walk the Park Avenue trail southward. Branch west on a climbers' path aimed at the formation, work up a gully beneath the lower walls, and swing around onto the benches on the tower's west side. Scramble slabs to the pedestal ledge at the base of the tower.

Start from the Mary's Rock trailhead in the far corner of the Panorama lot and climb the trail 1.7 steep miles to the cliffs. The tops of the cliffs lie 0.1 mile on at the summit; for the bases, turn left off the summit path and walk about 50 yards.

Find the trail at the right edge of the prominent turnout on the road, about half a mile above the Squire Creek Pass trailhead; it starts behind a big alder and can be hard to spot. Gloves help on this roughly 30 minute climb through slide maple and devil's club, which ends at the foot of the first tooth.

Reach the foot of Hidden Falls, where the Cascade Canyon trail begins, by crossing Jenny Lake on the boat from the south-end dock, or by hiking the trail around the lake's south shore past Moose Pond. A third option is to walk around the lake's north and northwest sides from the String Lake bridge.

From the biggest lot on the right below the steep church switchback, find the obvious climbers' trail. It begins low and fades, with cairns marking its rising rightward traverse beneath the northern spires. Scramble slabs under Christianity Tower, then finish up the gully to the notch between it and Streaker Spire, about 30 to 40 minutes.

Start up the Old Big Oak Flat Road, heading north up the hill until you meet the main roadbed, which slants gently west. Follow it past the talus below Nuts Only Wall and Little Wing, then on to a railing above the Last Resort Cliff. Continue about ten more minutes; the buttress sits hidden in the trees directly above.

Take the Old Big Oak Flat Road: walk north up the hill to the main roadbed that slants gently west. Ten to fifteen minutes along it, sometimes beneath rockslides, brings you to open talus slopes under the Nuts Only Wall.

Follow the blocked old road south of the turnout to an abandoned stone quarry and skirt it on the left to reach a ridge heading toward Mt. Watkins. Stay on it for about a mile until YaSoo's bare summit shows on your left, then drop through the brushy gully between that summit and the Watkins ridge to the routes.

From the southwest corner of the day-use lot, walk the road to the Visitor Center, a little over three-quarters of a mile. Cross the bridge over Malibu Creek and pick up the Gorge Trail just beyond it. Follow it upstream about a quarter mile to the pool.
From the four-way trail intersection below the Sacred Cliffs, follow the Green Mountain West Ridge Trail uphill. The trail is very steep, and Ramp Rock appears beside it after roughly five minutes.

From the Glacier Gorge lot, follow the trail past Alberta Falls to the junction at about 1.75 miles, then keep on to Mills Lake and along its east shore up the valley to Black Lake, roughly five miles in. Above the lake the path gets rougher: climb the gully southeast of the lake, then follow cairns west across open slabs and tundra to the saddle with the spire.

Hike to the top of the Harmon Cave Trail, then cut southwest across the talus to a faint gap in the spine. You have the right spot when Overhang Rock's main summit lines up with the National Center for Atmospheric Research building. Scramble through the notch, then continue about 200 feet up and southward, keeping to the ridge's western flank, to reach the tall, steep west face.

From the Monument Canyon trailhead, drop down the trail about 600 feet to the canyon floor. Continue around the big spire that has a chimney splitting it below the summit, to its northwest side, then scramble up the scree to the base of the tower.

From the open camping spot just past the old quarry, set off from its north end heading north and downhill. The path bends east around the ridge and then rises up the flank of the following one, continuing east. The Approach Boulder sits uphill on your right and Cracked Wall is almost straight ahead.

From the dead-end Chair Rocks lot, walk west down the old road toward Spoof Rock. About 100 feet along, leave it and follow a game trail north, staying below the rocks on the ridgetop, to reach Upper Gemstone. Lower Gemstone lies a bit farther downhill from there.

From the big Auxier Ridge lot, walk back up the entrance road about 100 feet to the old gravel road and follow it roughly half a mile to a left-hand turn, the third one, just a few hundred feet beyond the Star Gap Arch turnoff. Take that trail half a mile past old campsites, then bear right along the ridge another half mile over some rocky stretches. When the orange buttress of Jailhouse Rock shows ahead on the right, go five more minutes and drop down a faint, steep trail to the wall.

From the parking area, hike straight back and cross the small creek, then head up the hill to reach the base of the 5.10 Wall. For the other walls, walk up the gravel road to a flight of stairs on the right and go up to reach the foot of the 5.11 Wall.

From the White Rock Springs lot, hike south on the White Rock to Willow Springs trail. After about five to ten minutes, strike off to the right, toward the northwest, aiming for the first big east-west wash. The crag sits on the south side of that wash.

Start at the Boat Launch lot and walk the fire road past the Fisherman Boulder until it narrows to a footpath and forks. Bear right and follow the trail behind the marsh by the Blair Woods Boulders. It winds around several marshes to a small pond with a big boulder in it, and the blocks lie on the far side. Plan on about 45 minutes in all.

Hike north on the Piedra Lisa Spring Trail to the junction where Juan Tabo Canyon meets Waterfall Canyon. The first streambed you cross is Waterfall Canyon. Turn right and follow it upstream on either bank, scrambling the steep spots, to the waterfall, about three-quarters of a mile with roughly 700 feet of gain.

From the Top Spur trailhead, drop down the trail for a minute to French's Dome. Then work uphill through the brush; Misty Slab is the sloping buttress about half an hour above the Dome and easy to spot.

From the Clear Creek parking area, follow the rim trail toward the prominent canyon point and bear left just before reaching it. After several hundred yards the trail splits; take the right fork down a short hop-down to the cliff base by Colorado Boy. Fox Wall lies about 80 yards downstream.
From the Devils Garden lot, take the trail toward Double O Arch, passing Landscape Arch on the way. Double O is about 2 miles in, and the spire stands another half mile or so to the north.

From the end of the shuttle road, follow the old abandoned road southwest to where it doubles back beside a big gully. Climb the gully up to the Phoneline Trail, walk west along it a few hundred feet over a saddle, then head up the next gully toward the wall.
From the Mesa Trail, walk about 60 feet north, then leave the path and climb northwest up the gully. The boulder sits roughly five minutes up the drainage.
From the parking beside the lodge, find the path that drops down to the Appalachian Trail. The cliffs sit directly below the lodge.
From the picnic area, follow the marked trail down the canyon for 1.3 miles to the waterfall. The climbable cliffs are across from the falls.
